import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.86

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is it true that the identical relations of a polycyclic group have a finite basis?

A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
in which every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic.

An *identical relation* (law) of $G$ is a word $w$ of the free group $F_\infty$ of countably
infinite rank such that $w$ is mapped to $1$ by every homomorphism $F_\infty \to G$, i.e. every
substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables of $w$ gives $1$. The identical relations of
$G$ form a fully invariant subgroup $V(G)$ of $F_\infty$. A set $B$ of words is a *basis* for
the identical relations of $G$ if $V(G)$ is the fully invariant closure of $B$ in $F_\infty$,
i.e. the verbal subgroup of $F_\infty$ generated by $B$: the subgroup generated by the images of
the words of $B$ under all endomorphisms of $F_\infty$. Equivalently, every identical relation
of $G$ is a consequence of the relations in $B$, so that the variety of groups generated by $G$
is defined by the laws in $B$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.86»

/--
A group `G` is *polycyclic* if it has a finite subnormal series
`⊥ = G₀ ⊴ G₁ ⊴ ⋯ ⊴ Gₙ = ⊤` (each `Gᵢ` normal in `Gᵢ₊₁`)
in which every factor `Gᵢ₊₁ ⧸ Gᵢ` is cyclic.
-/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (s i.succ ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))

/--
The *identical relations* (laws) of a group `G`: the words `w` of the free group `FreeGroup ℕ`
of countably infinite rank such that `φ w = 1` for every homomorphism `φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`,
i.e. every substitution of elements of `G` for the variables of `w` gives `1`.
-/
def laws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨅ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ.ker

/--
The *verbal subgroup* (fully invariant closure) of `FreeGroup ℕ` generated by a set `S` of
words: the subgroup generated by the images of the words of `S` under all endomorphisms of
`FreeGroup ℕ`. It is the smallest fully invariant subgroup of `FreeGroup ℕ` containing `S`, and
consists of the words that are consequences of the words in `S`.
-/
def verbalClosure (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure (⋃ ψ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, ψ '' S)

/--
The identical relations of a group `G` *have a finite basis* if there is a finite set `S` of
words such that the identical relations of `G` are exactly the words of the verbal subgroup
generated by `S`.
-/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), S.Finite ∧ laws G = verbalClosure S

/--
Is it true that the identical relations of a polycyclic group have a finite basis?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.86» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPolycyclic G → HasFiniteBasisOfLaws G := by
  sorry

/- ## Basic API for the definitions -/

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic (take the series of length `0`). -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPolycyclic.of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- Cyclic groups are polycyclic (take the series `⊥ ≤ ⊤`). -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPolycyclic.of_isCyclic [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  refine ⟨bot_le, ?_⟩
  have : ((⊥ : Subgroup G).subgroupOf ⊤).Normal := by
    rw [Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]; infer_instance
  exact ⟨this, isCyclic_of_surjective _ (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)⟩

/-- Every word is an identical relation of the trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem laws_eq_top_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] : laws G = ⊤ := by
  simp [laws, Subgroup.eq_top_iff', MonoidHom.mem_ker, Subsingleton.elim _ (1 : G)]

/-- The commutator word `[x₀, x₁]` is an identical relation of every commutative group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem commutator_mem_laws {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] :
    ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ ∈ laws G := by
  simp [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, map_commutatorElement,
    commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm, mul_comm]

/-- The identical relations of a group form a fully invariant subgroup of `FreeGroup ℕ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_laws_le (ψ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ) : (laws G).map ψ ≤ laws G := by
  rintro _ ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, SetLike.mem_coe] at hw ⊢
  exact fun φ => hw (φ.comp ψ)

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by a set of words is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_verbalClosure_le (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (ψ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ) :
    (verbalClosure S).map ψ ≤ verbalClosure S := by
  rw [verbalClosure, MonoidHom.map_closure]
  refine Subgroup.closure_mono ?_
  simp only [Set.image_iUnion, Set.image_image, Set.iUnion_subset_iff]
  intro ψ'
  exact Set.subset_iUnion_of_subset (ψ.comp ψ') fun x hx => by simpa using hx

/-- A set of words is contained in the verbal subgroup it generates. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subset_verbalClosure (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : S ⊆ verbalClosure S :=
  (Set.subset_iUnion_of_subset (MonoidHom.id _) (by simp)).trans Subgroup.subset_closure

end Kourovka.«1.86»

/-- The identical relations (group laws) of `G`, viewed as a subgroup of the free group
of countable rank. A word is a law when every assignment of its variables in `G`

  one_mem' := by simp
  mul_mem' := by

    simp [hx f, hy f]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro x hx f
    simp [hx f]

intersection of all subgroups that contain `S` and are stable under every endomorphism
of the free group. -/
def verbalClosure (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  sInf {N : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) |
    S ⊆ N ∧ ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, N.map φ ≤ N}

/-- A group is polycyclic if it has a finite ascending subnormal series with cyclic
factors. In the last clause, `x` generates the factor `P (i + 1) / P i`: every element
of `P (i + 1)` differs from an integral power of `x` by an element of `P i`. -/

  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ P : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G,
    P 0 = ⊥ ∧ P (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n,
        P (Fin.castSucc i) ≤ P (Fin.succ i) ∧
        Subgroup.Normal ((P (Fin.castSucc i)).subgroupOf (P (Fin.succ i))) ∧
        ∃ x ∈ P (Fin.succ i), ∀ y ∈ P (Fin.succ i),
          ∃ z : ℤ, y * (x ^ z)⁻¹ ∈ P (Fin.castSucc i)

/--
Is it true that the identical relations of every polycyclic group have a finite basis?

Here the identities are words in the free group of countable rank. A finite basis is a
finite set of words whose fully invariant (verbal) closure is the subgroup of all
identities of the group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.86» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPolycyclic G →
      ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), S.Finite ∧ verbalClosure S = identities G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.86»
modeling_decisions: The implicit quantifier is formalized universally over all groups `G : Type` satisfying the problem-local predicate `IsPolycyclic`.

Group identities are represented as a subgroup of `FreeGroup ℕ`; membership means evaluation to `1` under every assignment `ℕ → G`. Thus the free group has countable rank and captures laws with arbitrary finite sets of variables.

A finite basis is represented by a finite set `S` of words whose `verbalClosure` equals the full identity subgroup. The closure is the intersection of all subgroups containing `S` and stable under every endomorphism of `FreeGroup ℕ`, i.e. the fully invariant subgroup generated by `S`.

Polycyclicity uses a finite ascending series from `⊥` to `⊤`. Each preceding subgroup is normal in the next via `subgroupOf`, and cyclicity of the factor is expressed directly by a coset generator: every element of the next subgroup differs from an integral power of one element by an element of the preceding subgroup. This avoids proof-dependent quotient typeclass instances while stating the standard cyclic-quotient condition.

namespace Kourovka.«1.86»

/-- For subgroups $H \leq K$, the factor $K/H$ is cyclic: $H$ is normal in $K$ and some
coset of $H$ generates every coset of $K/H$. -/
def IsCyclicFactor {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  H ≤ K ∧
    (∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ K, y * x * y⁻¹ ∈ H) ∧
    ∃ g ∈ K, ∀ x ∈ K, ∃ z : ℤ, x * (g ^ z)⁻¹ ∈ H

/-- A group is polycyclic if it has a finite subnormal series from the trivial subgroup to the
whole group whose factors are cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G,
    H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, IsCyclicFactor (H i.castSucc) (H i.succ)

/-- The subgroup of identical relations (group laws) of $G$ in the free group on countably many
variables. A word is in this subgroup exactly when every evaluation of its variables in $G$ is
trivial. -/
def identities (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨅ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f.ker

/-- The fully invariant (verbal) subgroup generated by a set of words: the subgroup generated by
all images of those words under endomorphisms of the countably generated free group. -/
def verbalClosure (s : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨆ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, (Subgroup.closure s).map f

/-- The identical relations of $G$ have a finite basis if their verbal subgroup is the fully
invariant closure of finitely many words. -/
def HasFiniteIdentityBasis (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ s : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), identities G = verbalClosure (s : Set (FreeGroup ℕ))

/--
Is it true that the identical relations of every polycyclic group have a finite basis?

Here a polycyclic group has a finite subnormal series with cyclic factors. Its identical
relations are the words in the free group of countable rank that evaluate to the identity under
every substitution in the group. A finite basis is a finite set of words whose fully invariant
(verbal) closure is the subgroup of all such relations.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.86» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPolycyclic G → HasFiniteIdentityBasis G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.86»

A cyclic factor K/H is expressed by H ≤ K, normality of H relative to K, and the existence of a coset whose integer powers represent every coset.

Identical relations are represented as the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms from the free group on ℕ to G; these homomorphisms are exactly evaluations of countably many variables in G.
The fully invariant verbal closure of a set of words is represented as the join of the images of the subgroup generated by those words under all endomorphisms of the countably generated free group.
A finite basis is a Finset of words whose verbal closure equals the full identity subgroup.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.86

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is it true that the identical relations of a polycyclic group have a finite basis?

An *identical relation* (law) of a group $G$ is a word $w$ in the free group
$F_\infty$ of countable rank such that $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every
substitution of elements of $G$ for the generators. The laws of $G$ form a
fully invariant subgroup of $F_\infty$. They have a *finite basis* if they are
the fully invariant (verbal) closure of finitely many words, i.e. if the
variety generated by $G$ is finitely based.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.86»

/--
A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
(each term normal in the next) all of whose factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ are cyclic.
-/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (↥(s i.succ) ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))

/-- Every cyclic group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  fin_cases i
  refine ⟨bot_le, ?_⟩
  simp only [Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, Fin.castSucc_zero, Matrix.cons_val_zero,
    Fin.succ_zero_eq_one, Matrix.cons_val_one, Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]
  exact ⟨inferInstance,
    isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.mk' _) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)⟩

/--
The *laws* (identical relations) of a group $G$: the words $w$ in the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` of countable rank such that $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every
substitution of elements of $G$ for the generators.
-/
def laws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨅ f : ℕ → G, (FreeGroup.lift f).ker

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_laws {G : Type*} [Group G] {w : FreeGroup ℕ} :
    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]

/-- The laws of a group form a fully invariant subgroup of the free group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem laws_map_le (G : Type*) [Group G] (φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ) :
    (laws G).map φ ≤ laws G := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap]
  intro w hw
  rw [Subgroup.mem_comap, mem_laws]
  rw [mem_laws] at hw
  intro f
  have h : (FreeGroup.lift f).comp φ =
      FreeGroup.lift fun i => FreeGroup.lift f (φ (FreeGroup.of i)) :=
    FreeGroup.ext_hom _ _ fun i => by simp
  have hw' := congrArg (fun ψ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G => ψ w) h
  simp only [MonoidHom.comp_apply] at hw'
  rw [hw']
  exact hw _

/--
The *verbal closure* (fully invariant closure) of a set $S$ of words in the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ`: the subgroup generated by all images of elements of $S$ under endomorphisms
of `FreeGroup ℕ`. It is the smallest fully invariant subgroup containing $S$; its elements
are exactly the consequences of the laws in $S$.
-/
def verbalClosure (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure (⋃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, φ '' S)

/-- Consequences of laws of $G$ are laws of $G$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalClosure_le_laws (G : Type*) [Group G] {S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)}
    (hS : S ⊆ laws G) : verbalClosure S ≤ laws G := by
  refine (Subgroup.closure_le _).2 (Set.iUnion_subset fun φ => ?_)
  rintro _ ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩
  exact laws_map_le G φ ⟨w, hS hw, rfl⟩

/--
Is it true that the identical relations of a polycyclic group have a finite basis?

That is, for every polycyclic group $G$, is there a finite set $S$ of words in the
free group of countable rank such that the laws of $G$ are exactly the fully invariant
(verbal) closure of $S$, i.e. the consequences of the finitely many laws in $S$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.86» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPolycyclic G →
      ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), laws G = verbalClosure ↑S := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.86»

namespace Kourovka.«1.86»

/-- For subgroups $H \le K$ of a group, the factor $K/H$ is cyclic if $H$ is
normal in $K$ and every coset of $H$ in $K$ is represented by an integral
power of one element of $K$. -/
def IsCyclicFactor {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  H ≤ K ∧ (H.comap K.subtype).Normal ∧
    ∃ x : K, ∀ y : K, ∃ n : ℤ, (x ^ n)⁻¹ * y ∈ H.comap K.subtype

/-- A group is polycyclic if it has a finite subnormal series with cyclic
factors. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G,
    H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, IsCyclicFactor (H i.castSucc) (H i.succ)

/-- A word in countably many variables is an identity (law) of a group if it
evaluates to the identity under every assignment of its variables. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/--
Is it true that the identical relations of every polycyclic group have a
finite basis?

A finite set $S$ of identities of $G$ is a basis here when every group that
satisfies all identities in $S$ also satisfies every identity of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.86» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPolycyclic G →
      ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ),
        (∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesIdentity G w) ∧
        ∀ (H : Type) [Group H],
          (∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesIdentity H w) →
          ∀ w, SatisfiesIdentity G w → SatisfiesIdentity H w := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.86»
modeling_decisions: A polycyclic group is represented by a finite ascending subnormal series from the trivial subgroup to the whole group, with each adjacent factor cyclic.

Cyclicity of an adjacent factor is stated directly by normality and the existence of an element whose integral powers represent every coset; this avoids requiring a quotient-group normality instance while retaining the standard meaning.
Identities are words in the free group on countably many variables that evaluate to the identity under every variable assignment.

A finite basis is expressed semantically: it is a finite set of identities of G such that every group satisfying that set satisfies every identity of G. By the standard equational semantics of groups, this is equivalent to generation under fully invariant/verbal closure.
